title: The star characterization conjecture for graphs with one large Laplacian eigenvalue
source: L. Emilio Allem, Antonio Cafure, Ezequiel Dratman, Luciano N. Grippo, Martín D. Safe and Vilmar Trevisan, “Partial characterization of graphs having a single large Laplacian eigenvalue”, arXiv:1710.01710 (2017). https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.01710
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with Laplacian eigenvalues $\mu_1\geq\cdots\geq\mu_n$ and average degree $\overline{d}(G)=2m/n$, where $m$ is the number of edges and $n$ the number of vertices. Define $\sigma(G)$ to be the number of Laplacian eigenvalues at least $\overline{d}(G)$. For integers $r\geq 1$ and $s\geq 0$, let $K_{1,r}+sK_1$ denote the disjoint union of the star $K_{1,r}$ and $s$ isolated vertices. **Star characterization conjecture.** $\sigma(G)=1$ if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $K_1$, $K_2+sK_1$ for some $s\geq 0$, or $K_{1,r}+sK_1$ for some $r\geq 2$ and $0\leq s<r-1$. The conjecture seeks a complete structural characterization of graphs having exactly one Laplacian eigenvalue at least their average degree; the paper proves it for several classes, including graphs whose complements are disconnected, but the general case remains open.
summary: A graph on n >= 1 vertices has exactly one Laplacian eigenvalue greater than or equal to its average degree (sigma(G) = 1, eigenvalues counted with multiplicity) if and only if n = 1, or G is K_{1,1} with any number s of isolated vertices, or G is a star K_{1,r} with r >= 2 together with s < r - 1 isolated vertices. No connectivity is assumed; for connected graphs this says that the stars are the only graphs with sigma = 1, the conjecture of Allem, Cafure, Dratman, Grippo, Safe and Trevisan, who proved it for forests, cographs, split graphs and other classes. The proof uses the bound mu_2 >= d_2 to reduce to connected graphs with a single vertex above the average degree, takes a Schur complement at that vertex, and closes the case by a degree-deficit count. Mathlib has no Courant-Fischer theorem, so Lean builds the link between counting eigenvalues above a threshold and subspaces on which the quadratic form is large, and proves the bound on the second largest Laplacian eigenvalue.
paste_summary: Proved. A graph has exactly one Laplacian eigenvalue at least its average degree if and only if it is a single vertex, K_{1,1} plus isolated vertices, or a star K_{1,r} (r >= 2) plus fewer than r - 1 isolated vertices. For connected graphs this is the conjecture of Allem et al. (arXiv:1710.01710, Electron. J. Combin. 2018) that the stars are the only graphs with sigma = 1.
caveat: Bounded literature search only; the journal texts were not all read. A 2022 paper (Ahanjideh, Akbari, Fakharan, Trevisan, Linear Algebra Appl. 632) states that stars are known to be the only connected graphs with sigma = 1; the cross-model reviewer traced that sentence to the 2017 conference version of the source, which only conjectures it, and judged it a mis-citation, but a reader may meet the sentence. The proof is elementary (about a page and a half beyond published bounds); the problem drew little attention after 2018 (cross-model confidence: 0.8 overall, not routine 0.70). The Lean endpoint is identical in statement to the one the cross-model reviewer required; root made that comparison, and no second cross-model lane read the finished Lean.
